To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) unbalanced growth, as measured by increased ratio of dsRNA to DNA, is a common feature of cells arrested at G1/S border; (2) unbalanced growth per s, as measured by increase in dsRNA/DNA, is not lethal; (3) unbalanced growth in the cells blocked in mid S phase is not lethal; and (4) unbalanced growth is not lethal in the daughter cells after progression through the S‐phase.

dsRNA/DNA ratios in cells blocked at or in early S phase were higher than in cells blocked at G0 or in late S phase; the dsRNA/DNA content in cells blocked at early S phase increased during the first 16–24 h of incubation and remained unchanged during the next 16–24h; cell viability in cultures blocked at early S‐phase decreased with time after the initial increase; the dsRNA content in cells progressed through S phase increased continuously;
dsRNA/DNA accumulation in HeLa S _{3} cells blocked by HU or TdR is characteristic of unbalanced growth, and that the accumulation is controlled by progression of cells through the S phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dsRNA in the cell cycle and cell death.
the relationship between the rate of cell proliferation, dsRNA accumulation and cell viability in HeLa S 3 cells blocked at the G1/S transition by HU or excess TdR.
the effect of cell cycle blockage on dsRNA accumulation in HeLa S _{3} cell cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the unbalanced growth in cells treated with DNA synthesis inhibitor is a result of the unbalanced growth per‐se, as well as a result of the cell cycle control mechanisms which are not fully effective in the cells with unbalanced growth.
unbalanced growth in HeLa S cells is not lethal for them, but the accumulation of dsRNA in the cell may be lethal for the cell.
the dsRNA/DNA ratios were not affected by cell proliferation and were not a function of the cell cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dsRNA accumulation is not directly related to cell death in He La S3 cultures treated by HU or excess TdR.
dsRNA accumulation is a normal phenomenon in cells and that the rate of accumulation is controlled by the rate of DNA synthesis.
dsRNA accumulates in cells during the cell cycle, but the rate of accumulation is dependent on the cell cycle progression and the rate of cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accumulation of dsRNA is not lethal per se, but rather is an indicator of unbalanced cell proliferation.
dsRNA accumulation is a normal process in mammalian cells.
dsRNA content in the cell is regulated in such a way as to prevent the unbalanced condition from developing during cell proliferation.
